title: Autotune defaults: batching/caching, quant profiles, and unit-econ tooling
author: Liam Chen
description: Motivation: reduce per-token unit cost for common workloads by providing safe, production-ready defaults for batching and prefix/KV caching, introducing quantization profiles for validated model variants, and exposing unit-economics tooling so SREs and platform engineers can make tradeoffs with clear cost/latency signals. This PR implements three coordinated pieces: 1) Autotune defaults for batching and caching policy that pick conservative but cost-saving values based on traffic shape, model size, and customer tier; 2) Quantization profile support that registers validated profiles (int8/4/4+ variants) with runtime fallback rules; 3) Unit-economics tooling: a lightweight service and console hook that simulates per-route token cost under candidate config changes and surfaces expected savings and latency impact. Changes: - runtime/autotune.py: new autotune engine that observes request histograms and recommends/sets defaults; includes safety gates (min-max batch, cold-start limits, warm-up period). - runtime/kv_cache_manager.py: cache policy extension to enable prefix-only caching by default for long-tail routes, with TTL heuristics. - runtime/quant_profiles.md and runtime/quant_registry.py: quant profile metadata + registration APIs + compatibility checking. - tooling/unit_econ/service.py: service to compute modeled unit economics given batching/caching/quant settings. - console/ui/unit_econ_widget.tsx: UI for route-level cost simulation and rollback A/B experiments. - infra/helm/values.autotune.yaml: defaults and toggles for Dedicated/Private deployments. - tests/*: unit and integration tests for autotune decision logic + quant-profile fallback. Checklist: - [x] Implement autotune engine and decision heuristics - [x] Add quant profile registry and validation harness - [x] Add unit-econ service and console integration - [x] Tests covering edge cases (cold-start, burst traffic) - [x] Docs: runtime/README + console docs - [x] Performance validation on staging (latency regression < 5% P95 for critical routes) Performance summary: in staging with mixed traffic (50% short-chat, 30% long-form, 20% embeddings) we observed a 22% reduction in per-token cost for CPU-bound routes and 12% for GPU-backed generation while keeping P95 latency regressions under 4% for primary routes. Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime.autotune.enabled; we will rollout to canary accounts for 48h with continuous monitoring of unit-econ delta, latency SLOs, and error rates. If unit-econ improves >10% without SLO violations we will expand. How to review: focus on autotune decision safety gates, quant-profile compatibility table, and unit-econ model assumptions (tooling/unit_econ/service.py). Tests: added deterministic unit tests for batching logic and integration tests that mock KV cache warm state. Related: ENG-2045 tracking autotune metrics and ENG-2067 product acceptance criteria. Notes: quant profiles are registered as metadata only; no automatic re-quantization of customer models is performed. This PR includes a migration step that adds a small DB table to register deployed quant profiles; migration has backward-compatible defaults and a cleanup path.

testing_instructions: Run pytest tests/autotune_test.py and tests/quant_profile_test.py; deploy helm chart with runtime.autotune.enabled=true to a staging cluster and exercise routes from tests/unit_econ_integration.py; check console Unit Econ widget under Settings > Routes.
notes: No breaking API changes. Migration adds quant_profiles table with backward-compatible defaults. Quant profiles only affect model selection/fallback and do not mutate stored customer model artifacts.
